title: Submission approve/reject has no authorization: any self-issued API key can review any submission
description:
SubmissionService.Review never receives the caller's identity. There is no actor parameter at all, and the emitted event hardcodes the actor:

  backend/app/smart_contract/services/submission_service.go:169  func (s *SubmissionService) Review(ctx, submissionID string, body SubmissionReviewInput)
  backend/app/smart_contract/services/submission_service.go:191  s.store.UpdateSubmissionStatus(...)  // no ownership check
  backend/app/smart_contract/services/submission_service.go:201  Actor: "reviewer"  // hardcoded

The REST route only wraps the handler in an API-key check, never an ownership check. The MCP surface has the identical gap in handleApproveSubmission / handleRejectSubmission (backend/mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1099).

Because API keys are self-serve, any anonymous caller can approve or reject any submission on the node. Approval gates payout and rework resolution, so this is the highest-impact finding in the review.

This is structural, not a missing guard clause: the reviewer identity is not plumbed into this layer, so the fix changes the service signature and both call sites (REST + MCP).

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: Review() takes an authenticated actor and rejects callers who are not the wish creator or an authorized reviewer. REST and MCP share one enforcement path. Emitted events record the real actor. Regression tests cover wrong-actor reject for both surfaces.
notes:
Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). Confirmed independently by maya. Two implementation details found during triage that should shape the fix:
(1) There is already a working pattern in-repo to copy rather than invent: requireAuthorizedApprover (mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1167), which the proposal approval path calls at :1061. The submission handlers should use the same helper.
(2) The MCP handlers already RECEIVE the caller identity and discard it -- handleRejectSubmission (:1099) and handleApproveSubmission (:1135) both take an apiKey parameter that is never referenced in the body. So on the MCP side this is a smaller fix than 'plumb identity through': the identity is in scope, just unused. The REST path (handleSubmissionReview -> SubmissionService.Review) is where the signature change is actually needed.
Room consensus: ship this first, together with irl.7.
IN PROGRESS 2026-09-13. Implemented by consolidating rather than patching twice, since enforceCreatorApproval (REST) and requireAuthorizedApprover (MCP) turned out to be ~55 lines of duplicated logic including the same irl.2 fail-open.

New app/smart_contract/authz.go:
  WishCreatorAuthorizer{Keys, Ingestion}.Authorize(apiKey, visibleHash, subject) - the single rule
  ProposalWishHash(proposal) / SubmissionWishHash(store, submission) - hash resolution
  Server.AuthorizeSubmissionReview(ctx, apiKey, submissionID) - exported so MCP shares it

Submission carries no wish reference, so resolution walks submission -> task -> contract and strips the 'wish-' prefix. Fails CLOSED when that chain breaks (no task, no contract), which is a new denial rather than a preserved fail-open - the irl.2 allowance only covers 'wish exists but has no creator_wallet'.

Call sites now: enforceCreatorApproval and requireAuthorizedApprover both delegate (each is a one-liner); handleSubmissionReview returns 403; handleApproveSubmission and handleRejectSubmission use the apiKey they were already discarding.

Side effect: irl.2's fail-open is now ONE branch in authz.go instead of two, so that bead is now a few-line change.

8 new tests in app/smart_contract/authz_test.go cover stranger denied, creator allowed, unbound key denied, unresolvable submission denied, missing submission denied, prefix stripping, wallet-binding requirement, global auditor. Full suite green, no regressions. NOT yet committed.
REVIEW 2026-09-13 by Sol in #stargate: current diff is NOT complete, do not commit. All blockers verified locally:

1. CONFIRMED (P0). Authorize still fails open when creator_wallet is unavailable (authz.go:40-52), so submission approve/reject is still bypassable for wishes with no recorded creator. Critically, the stego reconcile path never writes creator_wallet (stego_reconcile.go:420-438 sets stego_image_cid, visible_pixel_hash, etc. but not creator_wallet), so EVERY peer-replicated / chain-reconciled contract lands in the fail-open branch. Only locally created wishes get it (inscription_handler.go:584,672). Sol's refinement is better than treating this as all-or-nothing: submission review must fail CLOSED now, while proposal approval may keep the compatibility allowance as an explicit separate policy until irl.2.

2. CONFIRMED. Reviewer identity is still not propagated. Review() has no actor param (submission_service.go:169) and still emits Actor: "reviewer" (:201). This bead's own acceptance criteria require the real actor to be recorded, so the criteria are not met.

3. CONFIRMED. MCP approve/reject authorize correctly but then call h.store.UpdateSubmissionStatus directly (http_mcp_server.go:1127, :1164), bypassing SubmissionService.Review and therefore skipping maybeResolveRework (:198) and event emission (:200). REST and MCP diverge on side effects, not just on authorization. Overlaps bead fhz.

4. CONFIRMED. Tests exercise AuthorizeSubmissionReview directly, so they prove the rule but NOT that the handlers call it. Need wrong-actor rejection through the REST route and the MCP tool, plus missing-creator denial for submission review.

5. PARTIALLY WRONG. http_mcp_server.go does have a gofmt diff, but it is pre-existing, not from this change: the only hunk is map-literal alignment in handleCreateProposal (~:1021) and the file already failed gofmt at HEAD. Fixing it is fine but is unrelated churn.

Sol confirmed hash resolution and the stranger/unknown-key denials are sound.
TRIAGE of Sol's review by maya (#stargate, 2026-09-13) - supersedes the blocker classification above:

BLOCKING (agreed by both): Sol #1 fail-open must not apply to submission review ('that is a payout gate'), and Sol #3 MCP must route through SubmissionService.Review rather than calling UpdateSubmissionStatus directly. Proposal approval MAY keep the irl.2 compatibility branch, but as an explicit policy rather than a shared default - so Authorize needs to distinguish its two callers instead of applying one rule to both.

NOT BLOCKING: Sol #2 (actor propagation) is downgraded by maya to a cheap follow-up - 'Authz closes the hole. Actor:"reviewer" is an audit gap. Fix it if the wallet is already in hand at Review; don't hold the commit for a string.' Since Authorize already resolves the bound wallet, threading it through is close to free, but it must not gate the commit. This overrides the 'acceptance criteria not met' framing in the note above: the audit-trail criterion moves to follow-up.

STILL REQUIRED: Sol #4 surface-level tests. maya's rationale is worth keeping - 'helper-only tests would have missed the MCP bypass', which is exactly what happened. Need wrong-actor denial through the REST route AND the MCP tool, plus missing-creator denial on submission review.

Agreed work list: fail closed on submissions, route MCP through Review, add both surface tests, gofmt.

PROCESS BLOCKER: maya cannot see authz.go - Sol reviewed a local diff and maya's tree is still at the pre-export state. She asked that the patch be pushed somewhere readable before commit. Eric has elected to keep this work on dev rather than a feature branch, and to control commits/pushes himself, so this is pending his decision, not an oversight.
close_reason: All four acceptance criteria verified against dev at 2ff6ac2, not assumed. (1) Review takes an authenticated actor: submission_service.go:195 signature includes ReviewActor. (2) REST and MCP share one enforcement path: SubmissionReviewGate built at authz.go:213 and http_mcp_server.go:248, and the MCP-side duplicate was deleted. (3) Events record the real actor: submission_service.go:239 emits the wallet the gate authorized. (4) Wrong-actor regression tests on both surfaces: TestRESTSubmissionReviewRejectsStranger and TestMCPApproveSubmissionRejectsStranger / TestMCPRejectSubmissionRejectsStranger, all passing. Landed across #1 (gate), #3 (ugs: enforcement inside the service plus real actor). Full suite green on dev, plain and -race, 21 packages each.

title: Harden authorization and network surface before exposing a node to untrusted networks
description:
Umbrella for findings from the 2026-09-13 review. The recurring theme is that *authentication* is permissionless by design (anyone can mint an API key via POST /api/auth/challenge + /api/auth/verify by signing with a self-generated Bitcoin key -- handlers/auth_handler.go:145,198) while *authorization* is largely absent, and several code paths deliberately fail open when a secret env var is unset.

Consequence: 'requires a valid API key' is currently equivalent to 'anonymous', so every route that checks only key validity is effectively unauthenticated. Children cover the specific gaps plus two non-auth hardening items on the same exposed surface.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: All child issues closed. A node bound to a public interface has no unauthenticated mutating endpoint and no endpoint whose authorization reduces to 'holds any self-issued API key'.
notes:
Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). AGREED SHIP ORDER from the room:
  1. irl.1 + irl.7 together -- actor/owner plumbing, reusing requireAuthorizedApprover (mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1167) rather than a new pattern
  2. irl.2 -- fail closed, same PR as the above
  3. irl.4 (pprof + /metrics) and irl.6 (tarball caps, incl. the :916 prefix check) -- cheap wins, do today
  4. irl.3 -- callback HMAC first, ingest-hash follow-up
Deferred: irl.5 standalone (P3, its extraction instance rides along with irl.6). Out of epic scope: a49 before the next storage change, x63 background.
SHIP ORDER SUPERSEDED by maya's final consolidated verdict in #stargate:
  irl.1  ->  irl.4 + irl.6  ->  irl.2 + irl.3  ->  irl.7  ->  a49
Differences from the order recorded above: irl.7 moves from 'same PR as irl.1' to fifth (see the note on that bead), and irl.4/irl.6 move ahead of irl.2/irl.3 as the cheap wins to land immediately after the payout hole. irl.5 is skipped outright rather than deferred - her words: 'No public nodes, SanitizePath already does it right. Touch those 4 sites only if we pass them anyway.' fhz, gkh and x63 are 'real, not urgent'.
close_reason: All 8 children landed on dev and independently verified: irl.1 (submission review authz + real actor), irl.2 (proposal approval fail-closed), irl.3 (ingest/callback fail-closed), irl.4 (pprof/metrics loopback-gated), irl.5 (SanitizePath on uploads/sandbox/block-image/tar), irl.6 (tarball entry/size/total caps), irl.7 (create_task + proposal PATCH/publish owner gates), irl.8 (rework request creator-only). Acceptance met: mutating endpoints no longer reduce to 'holds any self-issued API key', and unset-secret paths fail closed.

title: on-chain confirm on this node must extract the sandbox
description:
osv.4 made extract an explicit POST /api/smart_contract/contracts/{id}/sandbox/pull and stripped it off confirm. That was the wrong product shape.

A replica that watches the chain and confirms a wish on-chain should unpack the sandbox tarball on that confirm. Otherwise /sandbox/<hash> is empty until a human remembers to POST pull. Confirm is the choice: this node saw settlement and is now hosting the tree.

Keep the rest of osv:

- Origin still creates the tarball at PreparePublishArtifacts (PSBT).
- Unconfirmed / unpaid must not unpack (downloadSandboxArtifacts already gates on status=confirmed).
- processEvent contract_confirmed must not extract (osv.1). That is local event fan-out, not the oracle.
- ReconcileSyncAnnouncement contract_confirmed must not extract (osv.1). Gossip is not this node's chain confirm.
- ReconcileStego / apply-from-local-file must stay metadata-only (osv.2). First-pass stego at 1-conf must not unpack unpaid work.
- Do not bring back the 22a/4u5 second-clock re-reconcile just to trip a confirmed-status branch inside stego. Call downloadSandboxArtifacts from the confirm path itself after ConfirmContract succeeds.

Hook points (this node, after the row is confirmed):

- maybeConfirmContract / promoteProvisionalProofs after a successful ConfirmContract
- promoteFundedContracts after a successful ConfirmContract
- markIngestionConfirmed / ensureMatchedContract when scanMayConfirm actually confirms
- the no-candidate OP_RETURN path after maybeConfirmContract

Need a handle on the smart-contract Server (or a narrow extract callback) from BlockMonitor. ConfirmContract on the store is status-only; the extract lives on Server.downloadSandboxArtifacts.

POST .../sandbox/pull can stay as a manual retry / origin no-op. It is not the replica's only door.

Tests that currently assert confirm-does-not-extract on the proof/funded paths have to flip for the on-chain confirm path only. Keep the gossip/stego tests that assert no extract.

Unconfirmed still refuses. processEvent, ReconcileSyncAnnouncement, and ReconcileStego still do not extract. POST .../sandbox/pull can stay as a manual retry. Tests pin: on-chain confirm extracts; gossip/stego confirm do not; unconfirmed still 409.

title: stego reconcile must not extract the sandbox tarball
description:
ReconcileStego / apply-from-local-file ends with:

  if contract status == confirmed { go downloadSandboxArtifacts }

That is how 22a and 4u5 make extract happen: they re-run stego reconcile after ConfirmContract so this branch fires. The first pass at 1-conf applies the payload and skips extract; the second pass unpacks.

Stego reconcile should apply the v2 payload (proposal, tasks, sandbox_hash, verified creator). It must not unpack the tarball. Delete the confirmed-status extract branch.

After this, reconcileOnChainArtifacts is metadata-only even if someone still calls it from the block monitor. The 22a follow-up hook then has nothing left to do (sibling bead).

Remove both go downloadSandboxArtifacts calls. mergeSandboxMetadata can stay: it only copies sandbox_hash / sandbox_tarball_cid onto the local row so a later explicit pull can find the file. Do not start the pull from the event.

title: Confirm must not unpack sandbox tarballs or distribute unsigned binaries
description:
Confirm marks a wish paid. It must not unpack a sandbox tarball or put unsigned binaries on disk for every replica.

PreparePublishArtifacts already creates the tarball at PSBT build and writes it under UPLOADS_DIR/<sandbox_hash>. That is the origin packing its own results so the hash can go in the stego payload and OP_RETURN. FinalizePublishArtifacts is optional IPFS/pubsub after that.

downloadSandboxArtifacts is the replica pull: find the hash-named tarball (disk or IPFS), verify, unpack to results/<id>. Idempotent if the tree is already there. The confirm check inside it is the right gate for a pull. Making confirm itself call the pull is the miss.

Today four paths auto-extract so the picture looks complete after settlement:

- server_events.go processEvent: contract_confirmed -> go downloadSandboxArtifacts
- ReconcileSyncAnnouncement contract_confirmed: merge metadata + download again
- stego_reconcile.go after applying a local stego file, if status is already confirmed
- stargate-22a / 4u5: reconcileConfirmedContractArtifacts after maybeConfirmContract / promoteFundedContracts, plus a second OP_RETURN reconcileOnChainArtifacts after scanMayConfirm, because the first reconcile ran at 1-conf and skipped extract

stargate-22a closed a real gap under the old goal (tarball never extracted on the task-proof path). That goal was wrong. Extract is distribution, not settlement. A node that unpacks on confirm is hosting unpaid work if the tx never settles, and is distributing unsigned binaries nobody asked this node to publish.

Keep create on PSBT. Keep confirm as confirm. Keep stego reconcile applying proposal/tasks/sandbox_hash from the on-chain image. Extract only when this node asks, and only after confirmed.
acceptance_criteria: Create stays on PreparePublishArtifacts (PSBT). Confirm only marks the row. Stego reconcile applies payload/metadata only. downloadSandboxArtifacts runs only on an explicit pull after confirmed. The four auto-extract hooks (processEvent, sync announce, reconcile confirmed-branch, 22a/4u5 post-confirm re-reconcile) are gone. Tests pin confirm-does-not-extract.

Filed 2026-09-14 after walking da058e2 with Eric. Opus/Cursor hung extract off settlement so the picture looked complete. Real split: origin creates at PSBT; replica extracts when they want a copy. Confirm is the gate on the pull, not the pull. Related closed work that assumed the old goal: stargate-22a, stargate-4u5 (promoteFundedContracts post-confirm reconcile), stargate-3p2.3 (catch-up confirming old heights would have re-extracted).
2026-09-15: Eric corrected the product shape. Confirm on this node should extract. osv.4 (REST pull only) was the wrong door; filed stargate-osv.5. osv.1/2/3 stay: do not extract from processEvent, sync gossip, or stego reconcile. Parent epic stays closed as history of the first landing.

Stego reconcile applies payload/metadata only. downloadSandboxArtifacts runs only on POST .../sandbox/pull after confirmed. The four auto-extract hooks are gone. Tests pin confirm-does-not-extract on processEvent, sync announce, ReconcileStego, proof confirm, and funded promote.

title: catch-up treats 6500-deep heights as settlement-ready and confirms old contracts
description:
settlementReady(height) compares the current tip to the block being processed. During catch-up the tip is 152464 and the height is 145xxx, so 20 confirmations is long since satisfied.

ensureMatchedContract, markIngestionConfirmed, maybeConfirmContract, and confirmContractTasks will therefore ConfirmContract / promote proofs on the historical height as soon as anything matches.

34a1e7b (22a) then re-runs stego reconcile and sandbox extract after that confirm. ae31475 ConfirmContract also adopts leftover wish- rows onto the bare VPH and force-supersedes the twin.

s.log in the 30min slice did not hit a match (only OP_RETURN without stego hash), so this path was not firing every block. It will fire the moment a historical tx matches one of the 305 fallback hashes, and it will rewrite confirmed_height to the old block.

Catch-up must not confirm or adopt at the scanned height. Confirm only when the monitor is within settlement depth of the live tip, or when the proof height is the height that originally funded the contract.
close_reason: ScanMayConfirm requires settlement depth AND tip-height <= N; catch-up writes provisional only. promoteProvisionalProofs still confirms near-tip proofs.

title: sequential catch-up starves the live tip so the UI never shows new blocks
description:
trackTip() processes currentHeight+1 sequentially with a 25-block batch. It will not process the live tip until the gap is closed.

s.log:

    btcd sync: blocks=152464 ... synced=true
    block monitor: catch-up progress current=146074 tip=152464 remaining=6390

At ~8s/block the remaining 6390 heights is about 14 hours. /api/data/block-summaries walks stored heights desc, so the scroller shows 146k as latest.

This is the intended no-skip-gap behavior from tipCatchupWindow (see tip_lag_test.go: jump to tip-3 skipped 144828). The missing piece is a second path that still records the live tip for the UI while backfill continues.

IndexBlock also sets heightsCache=nil on every processed height. During catch-up that is every 8s, so each UI poll does a full WalkDir. block-summaries is 1.6-1.7s in the same log.

Should process or at least index the live tip independently of historical backfill, and not invalidate the heights cache on every backfill height.
close_reason: trackTip still backfills sequentially but also ProcessBlock(live tip) without advancing currentHeight; IndexBlock inserts into heightsCache instead of wiping it.

title: oracle reconcile ListRecent pulls image_base64 on every block
description:
reconcileOracleIngestions calls ingestion.ListRecent(\"\", 500) for every ProcessBlock, including 1-tx empty blocks. ListRecent selects image_base64:

    SELECT id, filename, method, message_length, image_base64, metadata, status, created_at

s.log shows 305 ingestions on every height and a flat ~8s between stego scan complete and proposalCandidates. Matching only needs hashes and metadata. Images are read from disk later via moveIngestionImage if a tx actually matches.

Hence SQLite is reading hundreds of PNG/JPEG blobs per block, CPU sits at 100%, and /api/open-contracts waits on the same lock (6-8s in the same log).

ListRecent used for oracle candidates should not select image_base64. Cache the candidate maps across heights when the ingestion/proposal/contract sets have not changed. Skip the full reload on 0-image blocks that also have no OP_RETURN.
close_reason: ListRecentMeta omits image_base64; oracle reconcile caches that list for 30s so catch-up does not reread 305 PNG blobs per block.

title: Block monitor catch-up saturates CPU and hides the live tip
description:
After the Sept 13-14 landings the node is not showing new tip blocks in the UI, CPU sits at 100%, and s.log is full of 145xxx heights while btcd is already at 152464.

s.log 2026-09-15:

    btcd sync: blocks=152464 headers=152464 peers=8 ibd=false progress=0 synced=true
    block monitor: catch-up progress current=146074 tip=152464 remaining=6390
    Successfully processed block 146097 in 8.659s: 6 txs, 0 images

Even 1-tx empty blocks take ~8s. Parse and stego scan are instant. The time is oracle reconcile reloading 305 ingestions + 170 proposals + 181 contracts on every height.

Children cover the per-block blob load, tip vs backfill split, historical ConfirmContract, the leftover wish- confirm path from ae31475, the unindexed ListContracts twin predicate, and the log line that reads like an internet download.

The raw-block fetch itself is local btcd. "Downloaded raw block N from chain backend" is BtcdBackend.GetRawBlockHex (getblockhash + getblock). Internet fallback only logs "Trying to download raw block N from https://...".

title: Submission rework has no authorization and resets an already-reviewed submission to pending_review
description:
Found while filing stargate-az6, which lists the rework event's hardcoded
"claimant" actor. Threading a real actor through requires authorization, and once
you look, there is none at all. Verified against dev at 2ff6ac2, not inferred.

handleSubmissionRework (server_proposals.go:294) decodes the body and calls
SubmissionService.Rework with no authorization of any kind. Rework
(submission_service.go:309) takes no actor: its signature is
(ctx, submissionID, SubmissionReworkInput). So any self-serve API key can act on
any submission.

Two distinct consequences, both confirmed by running it:

1. Deliverables of another claimant's submission can be overwritten. Reviewers
   approve based on deliverables, so this is tampering with the artifact the
   review decision rests on.

2. Status is reset to pending_review unconditionally, with no source-state gate.
   A submission already approved, or already rejected, resets to pending_review.
   Confirmed for both: seeded approved -> Rework succeeded -> pending_review, and
   the same for rejected.

Consequence 2 undoes a completed review decision, which is the gate irl.1 and ugs
spent two PRs hardening. It also desynchronizes the cascade: approval sets task
approved and claim complete (policy_submission_status.go:56), and Rework only
calls UpdateSubmission, so the submission returns to pending_review while its
task stays approved and its claim stays complete. The submission can then be
reviewed again from that inconsistent state.

Not yet traced, and deliberately not asserted: whether a second approval from
that state produces a second payout. Payout appears to key on task status via the
PSBT path (server_psbt.go:1226) rather than on the submission, so a double payout
is not established. Someone should trace it before deciding priority; if it does,
this is P0 rather than P1.

The likely rule is claimant-only plus a source-state gate, but who may rework and
from which states is a product decision, not something to infer from the code.
Confirm the intended lifecycle before implementing.

This subsumes the rework "claimant" actor listed in az6; az6 keeps Approve and
the two proposal_create actors.
acceptance_criteria: Rework takes an authenticated actor and refuses callers who are not the submission's claimant. Enforcement lives in SubmissionService.Rework, not the handler, matching Review after ugs. Rework refuses a submission that is not in a reworkable state instead of resetting any status to pending_review; the allowed source states are written down. The rework event records the authorized identity rather than the literal "claimant". Regression tests cover a non-claimant refusal and an approved submission refusing to reset, each asserting the deliverables and status were not changed.
close_reason: Landed on dev via PR #14 (merge 3b2066c, commit aafb456). Rework is claimant-only through SubmissionReworkGate, fails closed when the gate is unwired, and a source-state gate allows only pending_review and reviewed so an approved submission can no longer be reopened (the double-payout path). Rework events name the authorized wallet. Mutation-checked independently: swallowing the authorization denial fails TestReworkDeniesBeforeMutating and TestRESTReworkRejectsNonClaimant; disabling the state gate fails TestReworkSourceStateGate, TestReworkRejectionNamesTheRouteBack and TestRESTReworkCannotReopenApprovedSubmission.

title: ProposalService.Approve trusts a creatorOK bool from its caller; four events still record fictional actors
description:
Follow-up to stargate-irl.7, agreed with maya in #stargate. Not an open exploit
today: REST is the only caller and it does authorize first. It is a structural
hole of the same kind irl.1/ugs closed for submission review.

1. Approve trusts its caller. proposal_service.go:150 is
   Approve(ctx, id, apiKey string, creatorOK bool). The only caller,
   server_proposals.go:100, runs enforceCreatorApproval and then passes the
   literal true. So authorization is a boolean argument, and any second caller
   that passes true is authorized by saying so. That is worse than a missing
   check because it reads as if a check happened. ugs removed exactly this shape
   from SubmissionService.Review; Approve kept it.

   Note Approve already receives apiKey, so it has what it needs to authorize
   itself. ProposalEditGate from irl.7 governs the same creator rule and can be
   reused directly rather than adding another authorizer.

2. Four events still name actors that no key corresponds to:
   - proposal_service.go:230 approve -> "approver"
   - proposal_service.go:288 proposal_create -> "creator"
   - proposal_service.go:391 proposal_create -> "creator"
   - submission_service.go:337 rework -> "claimant"

   irl.7 fixed update ("editor") and publish ("approver"); ugs fixed review.
   These four are the remainder. The approve one matters most: approving a
   proposal is money-adjacent and the record cannot say which key did it.

   The two proposal_create actors may be legitimately unresolvable if creation
   has no authenticated wallet in every path. If so, the outcome is to write
   down why rather than to invent an actor; a literal "creator" that is
   sometimes true and sometimes false is worse than an explicit unknown.

Sequencing: 1 and 2 are one change for approve, since the wallet needed for the
event is what the internal authorization returns. Do not split them.
acceptance_criteria: Approve authorizes internally through ProposalEditGate (or equivalent) instead of accepting creatorOK, and the parameter is deleted so no caller can assert its own authorization. The approve event records the wallet the authorizer accepted. The three remaining fictional actors are replaced with the identity that was actually authorized, or the reason they cannot be is written down. Wrong-actor test calls Approve directly, with no handler, and a mutation removing the internal check fails it.
close_reason: Landed on dev via PR #16 (merge 77c87c8, commit e253f67). Approve enforces authorization internally instead of trusting a creatorOK bool from its caller; approve and proposal_create events record the resolved wallet. NOTE: originally PR #13, which read MERGED but stranded into fix/irl7-owner-checks (cc780b6) and never reached dev; ee35c7a is still not an ancestor of dev. Content landed via cherry-pick in #16, not via #13. Mutation-checked: neutralizing the approve gate fails TestProposalApproveRefusesWhenAuthorizerMissing, TestProposalApproveDeniesBeforeMutating and TestRESTProposalApprovalDeniesMissingCreator.

title: Enforce submission review authorization inside SubmissionService.Review and record the real actor
description:
Follow-up to stargate-irl.1, raised by Sol and confirmed by maya on PR #1. Both
items were deferred deliberately during that PR, not missed. Neither is an open
exploit on the two surfaces that exist today; both are real remaining holes.

1. Authorization lives in the callers, not the service.

   REST handleSubmissionReview (server_proposals.go) and the MCP
   approve/reject handlers (http_mcp_server.go) each call
   Server.AuthorizeSubmissionReview / authorizeSubmissionReview and then call
   SubmissionService.Review. Review itself takes no authenticated actor and
   enforces nothing, so it is callable without an ownership check. Any third
   caller added later - a new tool, a job, a CLI path - gets no protection and
   nothing fails loudly to say so.

   The fix is to push enforcement into Review, so the check cannot be omitted
   by construction rather than by convention. That means Review needs the
   caller identity, which is the same plumbing item 2 needs.

2. Review events hardcode Actor: "reviewer".

   submission_service.go emits smart_contract.Event{..., Actor: "reviewer"}
   regardless of who acted, so the audit trail cannot answer "who approved this
   payout". The authenticated wallet is available at both call sites and is
   discarded.

Doing these together is the point: both need an actor threaded into
SubmissionService.Review, so splitting them means doing that plumbing twice.

Suggested shape (not prescriptive):
  Review(ctx, submissionID, input, actor) where actor carries the authenticated
  wallet; Review authorizes internally via the existing WishCreatorAuthorizer
  and emits Actor: <wallet>. Callers stop pre-authorizing and simply pass who
  they authenticated. Keep the DenyOnMissingCreator / AllowOnMissingCreator
  distinction from irl.1 intact - submissions must stay fail-closed.

Tests worth having, since irl.1 showed helper-level tests miss exactly this
class of gap:
  - Review with no actor, or an actor that does not own the wish, is refused
    even when called directly, not through a handler
  - the emitted event names the authenticated wallet, not "reviewer"
  - the REST and MCP surface tests added in irl.1 still pass unchanged, proving
    the move did not alter behaviour at the surfaces

Context: irl.1 was merged (or is being merged) as an incremental fix with both
of these known-open. Do not treat irl.1's acceptance criteria as met by that
PR; Sol flagged precisely this and maya's call was to keep irl.1 open through
merge and split these out here.
close_reason: Landed on dev via PR #3 (0813360). Authorization moved into SubmissionService.Review with a ReviewActor carrying only the API key; SubmissionReviewGate is built by both REST and MCP; the review event records the wallet the gate authorized instead of the literal "reviewer". A nil authorizer refuses rather than proceeding. Service-level tests call Review with no handler involved, and each guarantee was mutation-checked.

title: create_contract_rework_request accepts any wallet-bound key as the wish creator
description:
Found while implementing irl.1. handleCreateContractReworkRequest (mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1628) correctly requires a wallet-bound API key and rejects a missing one (:1645, :1655), but it never checks that the wallet is the wish creator before recording it:

  requester = keyInfo.Wallet                       (:1650-1653)
  h.store.CreateContractReworkRequest(ctx, contractID, requester, notes)   (:1659)

ContractReworkRequest.Requester is documented in core/smart_contract/types.go:62 as 'wallet address of wish creator', so the field's contract is being violated: any self-issued key can file a rework request against any contract and be recorded as its creator. Same class as irl.1 and irl.7 - a permissionless key performing a workflow-significant write.

Rework requests feed SubmissionService.maybeResolveRework, so this is workflow-affecting rather than cosmetic.

Now cheap to fix: irl.1 introduced WishCreatorAuthorizer in app/smart_contract/authz.go, shared by REST and MCP. This should resolve the contract's wish hash (strip the 'wish-' prefix from contract_id, same as SubmissionWishHash does via task) and call Authorize before creating the request.
acceptance_criteria: handleCreateContractReworkRequest authorizes the caller as the wish creator via WishCreatorAuthorizer before recording the request, and a non-creator wallet is rejected. Test covers the stranger-wallet case.
close_reason: Landed on dev via #23 (a4e1885, merge 2a36a28); ancestor-checked. Both surfaces refuse a non-creator before writing: the bead named the MCP tool, but REST at server_contracts.go had the identical hole, resolving the caller's own wallet and storing it as the requester. Authorization lives in ContractReworkService via ReworkRequestGate, which resolves the contract to its wish hash with ContractWishHash and defers to WishCreatorAuthorizer, so there is no second notion of wish ownership. Nil authorizer refuses. Recorded requester is the wallet the authorizer returned, not one the caller resolved alongside the check. Filing now emits contract_rework_requested naming that wallet; neither surface recorded anything before. handleResolveContractRework already required the original requester, so it was only ever as strong as creation was. Mutation-checked: trusting the key's wallet again turns all four REST deny cases and the MCP deny case into a 201 recording the impostor as requester.

title: AGENTS.md tells every agent to run `bd sync`, which does not exist in bd 1.2.2 - beads JSONL silently stopped exporting
description:
Root cause of the stale .beads/issues.jsonl, requested by maya in #stargate.

AGENTS.md instructs agents to run `bd sync` in six places, including 'Always run `bd sync` at session end' (:450) and 'Always `bd sync` before ending session' (:478), plus :15, :198, :441, :466-468. That command does not exist in bd 1.2.2:

  $ bd sync
  Error: unknown command "sync" for "bd"

So every agent that followed the documented workflow ran a failing command at session end, believed it had synced, and never exported. AGENTS.md:106 also claims bd 'exports to .beads/issues.jsonl after changes (5s debounce)', which did not happen either.

Observed damage: the committed JSONL was last written Jul 17 and holds 43 records, all closed, all stargate-*. The live Dolt DB on this machine holds 223. A fresh clone or an unhydrated DB therefore shows a project with zero open work.

This is not cosmetic - it already cost a real triage cycle. maya independently reviewed this repo on 2026-09-13, could not see any of the 12 review beads, and reasonably concluded from `bd doctor` plus the 43-closed JSONL that the tree was in fresh-clone state with an empty Dolt backend. Correct diagnosis of a misleading artifact.

The correct command is `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`.

Related: maya's local bd is 0.62.0 vs 1.2.2 here, which is why her `bd prime` and hook PATH checks also fail. Version skew across agents is part of the same problem.
acceptance_criteria: All `bd sync` references in AGENTS.md replaced with `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl` (or whatever the supported flow is), and the '5s debounce auto-export' claim at :106 either verified or corrected. A pinned minimum bd version is documented so agents do not run 0.62.0 against a 1.2.2 database. Ideally a pre-commit or CI check fails when the Dolt row count and the committed JSONL row count diverge, so this cannot silently recur.
notes: DECISION on origin/beads-sync (maya, #stargate): leave the 8 open starlight-* beads where they are. Do NOT import that branch in order to close them. Verified stale - all 8 refactors already landed on dev (data_api.go 2058->119, block_monitor.go 2967->426, handlers.go->52, middleware/smart_contract/server.go removed in favour of app/smart_contract/server.go at 199, InscriptionModal.jsx 2327->1346, DeliverablesReview.jsx 1239->712, psbt_builder.go 449). Recording so this is not re-litigated: the branch is a 362-record starlight-prefixed fossil, not live work, and must not be merged as such.
close_reason: Fixed on dev. Verified on origin/dev: AGENTS.md:108 now explicitly says not to run bd sync and not to rely on automatic export, directing agents to bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl instead. The command does not exist in bd 1.2.2, which is why the JSONL had silently stopped updating.

title: MCP create_proposal and approve_proposal bypass the ProposalService that REST uses
description:
The same operation is maintained twice with separate logic:

  REST  backend/app/smart_contract/server_proposals.go:117 -> proposalSvc.Create (services/proposal_service.go:216)
  MCP   backend/mcp/http_mcp_server.go:921  reimplements validation and budget logic inline against store.CreateProposal
  MCP   backend/mcp/http_mcp_server.go:1044 approve_proposal lists ALL proposals and linear-searches, then calls store.ApproveProposal directly

Every proposal or budget rule now needs fixing in two places, and the two have already drifted. This also matters for the authorization work in the security epic: two paths means two places to add each check.

claim_task already delegates to ClaimService (http_mcp_server.go:861), so the intended direction is established -- this is finishing it, not inventing it. The linear search at :1044 is also a straightforward O(n) fix via a direct lookup.

Context: backend/mcp/http_mcp_server.go is 2927 lines (tool switch at :676, chat hub, session state and per-tool handlers in one file); extracting the proposal handlers is a reasonable first slice if a split is wanted later.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: MCP create_proposal and approve_proposal call the same service layer as REST, with no duplicated validation or budget logic. approve_proposal looks the proposal up directly instead of scanning all proposals. A shared test asserts identical behaviour across both surfaces.
notes:
Scoped 2026-09-13 after az6 landed. Verified on dev@3b2066c.

Authorization is NOT the gap. MCP handleApproveProposal calls requireAuthorizedApprover, which uses the same WishCreatorAuthorizer as REST and has been fail-closed since irl.2. That is real defense in depth: the mcp package stays green when the az6 service gate is mutated away, because MCP does not depend on it.

The gap is behavioural divergence. handleApproveProposal calls store.ApproveProposal directly (http_mcp_server.go:1095) instead of ProposalService.Approve, so it is a second approve implementation that has drifted. It skips four things the service does:

1. No audit event. The service emits Event{Type: approve, Actor: wallet}. MCP emits nothing, so an MCP approval leaves no record of who approved. This silently undercuts the actor-naming work in ugs and az6 on exactly the path that has no other audit trail.
2. No fundraiser payout binding. For raise_fund proposals the service derives payout_address and funding_address from the API key's bound wallet and FAILS when there is no binding. MCP skips this, so an MCP-approved fundraiser can reach approved with no payout address where REST refuses. This is a real bug, not a smell, and is the reason to raise this from P2 to P1.
3. No BuildTasksFromMarkdown when Tasks is empty.
4. No archiveWish.

create_proposal has the same shape and should be checked in the same pass.

Fix: route both MCP handlers through ProposalService with a ProposalActor, the same way ugs did for submission review, and delete the duplicated pre-checks so there is one enforcement point. Surface tests should assert the approve event exists with the right actor, and that an MCP-approved raise_fund proposal without a wallet binding is refused.

Owner: Cursor, assigned by Eric. Not started; queue was drained first.
close_reason: Both halves landed on dev. approve_proposal routed through ProposalService.Approve in #19 (72d7f4b, 9be3ec5); create_proposal in #21 (a862541), plus the %w wrap fix Maya caught in review (a0932cf) without which the create Kinds were classified as empty. Verified by content on dev, not by merge status: all markers present, all four validation wraps are %w with no %v left, and go test -race ./... is green on 5fb697d. Divergences closed: contract_id shape, the missing proposal_create event, and store-refusal classification by sentinel instead of message text. create_proposal's contract_id changed from wish-<hash> to the bare hash; historical rows are not migrated.

title: Consolidate dual wiring: storage.NewAllStores and container.NewContainer build two independent data layers
description:
main() builds a data layer via storage.NewAllStores (backend/stargate_backend.go:284-306), then runHTTPServer builds a second one via container.NewContainer, which re-reads the environment from scratch (backend/container/container.go:46-115). The two are then mixed:

  backend/stargate_backend.go:841  blockMonitor.SetIngestionService(container.IngestionService)
  backend/stargate_backend.go:~845 StartIPFSIngestionSync(ctx, ingestionSvc, ...)   // the *other* service

So the block monitor and the IPFS ingest sync operate through different ingestion handles over the same data, which can disagree if one pool fails and the other succeeds -- exactly the class of bug that is impossible to reproduce. Relatedly allStores.ContractCache is allocated and never used (storage/factory.go:45), because handlers consume container.ContractCache instead.

The NewAllStores factory is the documented intended single source of truth (storage/factory.go:38) and epic stargate-ood phase 7 aimed to land this; the migration is still incomplete. Config sprawl is the supporting symptom: 124 distinct os.Getenv names across ~243 call sites and 50 files, including near-duplicate keys like STARGATE_SYNC_ENABLED vs STARGATE_SYNC_ENABLE.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: One data/ingestion layer is constructed once and injected everywhere. container.NewContainer no longer re-reads storage env vars. Block monitor and IPFS ingest sync share one ingestion service. No unused store is allocated. Duplicate env keys collapsed to one name with a deprecation alias.
notes: Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). Independently confirmed by maya: NewAllStores and container.Build each spin up their own ingestion service. Room consensus on sequencing: real and worth doing, but schedule it before the next storage-layer change rather than treating it as a security fire. Should not block the irl.* hardening PRs.
close_reason:
Fixed: NewContainer now takes *storage.AllStores and rebuilds nothing.

What was verified before changing anything:
- NewContainer re-read STARGATE_STORAGE, STARGATE_PG_DSN/DATABASE_URL, STARGATE_DATA_DIR and CONTRACT_CACHE_* and built its own ingestion service, data storage and contract cache.
- The ingestion DSN it derived was not the same one NewAllStores uses. It preferred the Postgres DSN whenever the environment carried it; NewAllStores only uses that DSN when cfg.Type is postgres. So with STARGATE_STORAGE=sqlite and a DATABASE_URL present the two layers addressed different databases.
- In that config initIngestionService retried the unreachable Postgres 5 times with increasing sleeps (~15s of startup stall) and then returned nil. The block monitor nil-guards bm.ingestion everywhere, so the visible effect was ingestion reconciliation silently never running -- confirmations never written back, wishes never reaching confirmed -- rather than a crash. That is the unreproducible failure this bead predicted, with a concrete trigger.
- The DataDir default was NOT divergent: both fall back to "data". That part of the original description was wrong.

Change:
- initializeMCPComponents returns *storage.AllStores whole instead of 5 unpacked pieces; unpacking was what left runHTTPServer with nothing to hand the container.
- runHTTPServer takes AllStores; its signature shrinks from 7 params to 3.
- NewContainer(stores *storage.AllStores) -- one arg. API key issuer/validator also come from AllStores now, so handlers cannot be given a different pair than the process authenticates with.
- initIngestionService deleted (dead, and the source of the 15s stall).
- blockMonitor.SetIngestionService now takes the same ingestionSvc the IPFS sync and wish GC use, not container.IngestionService.
- AllStores.ContractCache is now the one the handlers read, so it is no longer allocated-and-unused.
- NewAllStores defaults a non-positive cache TTL/size. Found by the new test: NewContractCache starts a ticker on the TTL and panics from inside its own goroutine on a non-positive interval, so a hand-built config took the process down. The factory has to be safe to call with a config built in code for injection to be viable.

Tests: container/container_single_layer_test.go asserts pointer identity of ingestion service, data storage and contract cache against AllStores, and that a postgres-flavoured environment cannot change what gets built. Mutation-checked by restoring the old internal construction: all four assertions fail, and the environment test reproduces the nil ingestion service.

Verification: build clean, go vet clean, go test -race ./... green across all packages.

Split out rather than done here: the config half of the acceptance criteria (duplicate env keys) is stargate-z6k -- mechanical, unrelated files. Found while writing the DI tests: stargate-ard, a documented Container.Close() that does not exist, so the cache and peer cleanup goroutines are never stopped.

title: Unauthenticated net/http/pprof handlers are exposed on all interfaces
description:
backend/stargate_backend.go:12   _ "net/http/pprof"   // registers on http.DefaultServeMux
backend/stargate_backend.go:710  mux.Handle("/debug/pprof/", http.DefaultServeMux)
backend/stargate_backend.go:635  http.ListenAndServe(":"+httpPort, handler)  // 0.0.0.0

No auth wrapper and no loopback restriction, so any publicly reachable node serves heap dumps, goroutine stacks and CPU profiles to anyone. That is both a DoS lever and a memory-disclosure risk on a process that handles wallet-adjacent data. The startup log at :618 advertises the endpoint as localhost, but nothing enforces that.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: pprof is off by default and enabled only via explicit opt-in env var, and when enabled is bound to loopback or placed behind admin auth. Default config exposes nothing under /debug/.
notes: Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). Scope expanded: /metrics has the same exposure and should be gated in the same change. stargate_backend.go:704 registers mux.Handle("/metrics", promhttp.Handler()) with no auth wrapper, on the same 0.0.0.0-bound mux as /debug/pprof/. Prometheus metrics leak node activity and topology to anonymous callers. Room consensus: cheap win, do today.
close_reason:
Landed on dev. Verified on origin/dev: registerDiagnosticRoutes gates both routes behind diagnosticsEnabled, which returns false unless the env is 1/true/yes/on, so default config registers nothing under /debug/ or /metrics. When enabled both are wrapped in middleware.LoopbackOnly, which reads r.RemoteAddr rather than X-Forwarded-For, so it is not header-spoofable behind a proxy. Scope expansion to /metrics is covered by the same function.

Also checked the residual the blank import implies: _ "net/http/pprof" registers on DefaultServeMux at init regardless of the gate, so a listener served with a nil handler would expose pprof around it. There is exactly one listener (stargate_backend.go:643) and it sets Handler explicitly, so DefaultServeMux is reachable only through the gated LoopbackOnly mount. title: Stego callback and /api/ingest-hash skip authentication entirely when their secret env var is unset
description:
Two ingestion entry points treat an empty secret as 'no auth required' rather than 'refuse to serve':

  backend/handlers/ingestion_handler.go:39  empty STARGATE_INGEST_TOKEN -> authorize() returns true

title: Extract smart-contract business rules from dialect stores into app/core services
description:
## Problem

Business rules for claims, submissions, proposal lifecycle, and contract status live **inside** three near-duplicate store implementations:

| File | ~LOC | Role |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `storage/smart_contract/sqlite_store.go` | 1.9k | durable SQLite |
| `storage/smart_contract/pg_store.go` | 2.3k | durable Postgres |
| `storage/smart_contract/memory_store.go` | 1.5k | tests / memory mode |

**~5.7k total**, much of it triplicated policy (status machines, idempotency, supersede rules), not dialect SQL.

That causes silent dialect drift (e.g. claim re-claim, approve conflict checks, “never demote confirmed wish”) and blocks `stargate-jh0` (GORM MCP CRUD): wrapping fat stores in GORM does not remove the second/third policy copy.

## Already extracted (do not redo)

Partial app/service work already exists — extend it, don’t parallel it:

- `app/smart_contract/services/ProposalService` — HTTP-facing create/list/approve orchestration; still calls fat `store.ApproveProposal` / `PublishProposal`
- `app/smart_contract/services/SubmissionService` — review/rework orchestration; still calls fat `store.UpdateSubmissionStatus`
- `app/smart_contract/services/TaskService` — commitment proof helpers only
- Shared pure helpers already in `storage/smart_contract/` (move or re-export from app/core as needed):
  - `PrepareProposalForCreate`, `ValidateProposalForApproval`, `NormalizeContractID`, `populateProposalTasks`, `BuildTasksFromMarkdown`, contract protection / supersede SQL fragments

## Target architecture

```
REST / MCP / sync
        │
        ▼
app/smart_contract/services/*   ← pure policy + orchestration (ONE place)
        │  uses thin Store CRUD + optional Tx
        ▼
storage/smart_contract.Store    ← row load/save, filters, transactions only
   Memory | SQLite | PG | (later GORM stargate-jh0)
```

**Rule of thumb:** if a function decides “is this transition allowed?” or “what side effects run?”, it belongs in `app/` (or pure package under `core/smart_contract`). If it only maps structs ↔ rows, it stays in storage.

## In-scope methods (high-churn, triplicated)

Extract in this priority order (each PR should keep all three dialects green):

### Wave 1 — claims & submissions (MCP hot path)
1. **`ClaimTask`** — status gate (`available`/`claimed`), active-claim conflict, same-wallet idempotency, claim TTL, `contractor_wallet` into merkle_proof, task row updates  
2. **`SubmitWork`** — claim active/submitted, expiry, submission row + claim/task status  
3. **`UpdateSubmissionStatus`** — approve/reject cascades (task + claim reset/complete)

### Wave 2 — proposal lifecycle
4. **`CreateProposal`** — use `PrepareProposalForCreate`; supersede wish contract only when eligible (confirmed/completed protected)  
5. **`ApproveProposal`** — pending-only, validation, sibling reject, dual-approve conflict on contract_id / visible_pixel_hash, supersede wish  
6. **`PublishProposal`** — approved→published; bulk task/claim status transitions

### Wave 3 — contract / wish integrity
7. **`ConfirmContract`** — confirmation fields, status  
8. **`DeleteWish` / rework request create-resolve** — status guards aligned with contract protection  
9. **`UpdateContractStatus` / `UpsertContractWithTasks`** — demotion rules vs confirmed wishes (see recent integrity hardening)

## Out of scope (this issue)

- Introducing GORM for MCP tables (`stargate-jh0` depends on this finishing first)
- Rewriting MCP tool handlers / REST surface for its own sake (they should call the new services; keep URLs/JSON stable)
- Ingestion / IPFS / stego reconcile policy (already mostly in `app/`; only touch if they bypass the new services with raw store status hacks)
- Full merge of Memory into sqlite `:memory:` (optional later)

## Dependencies

- **Discovered-from:** `stargate-e4z` (GORM foundation for keys/blocks — done)
- **Blocks:** `stargate-jh0` (MCP GORM CRUD) — mark dep when x7y waves land enough for thin repos
- **Related:** contract protection / dual-wish hardening on `dev` (must preserve in extracted rules)

## Suggested PR breakdown

| PR | Deliverable | Exit signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `ClaimPolicy` + service; stores become transactional CRUD used by service | sqlite+memory tests for claim idempotency/conflict identical |

## Design notes

### Package layout (proposed)

```
backend/core/smart_contract/     # pure types + pure transition helpers (no I/O)
  transitions.go                 # ClaimTaskInput → ClaimDecision, ApproveDecision, etc.
  status.go                      # allowed task/claim/proposal/submission statuses

backend/app/smart_contract/services/
  claim_service.go               # NEW — Claim / SubmitWork
  proposal_service.go            # EXTEND — move store-side approve/publish body here
  submission_service.go          # EXTEND — move cascade logic here
  contract_service.go            # NEW — Confirm / status / wish delete

backend/storage/smart_contract/
  store.go                       # SPLIT or document: “fat” methods thin out over time
  # Prefer adding narrow CRUD methods rather than growing Store forever:
  #   GetTaskForUpdate, InsertClaim, UpdateTaskClaimFields, ...
  # Or keep Store methods as facades that call shared policy + dialect exec
  # during migration (strangler), then delete facade bodies.
```

### Strangler pattern (required)

Do **not** delete `SQLiteStore.ClaimTask` on day one while MCP still type-asserts stores.

1. Extract pure decision function (table-driven tests, no DB).  
2. Implement once in service using existing store read/write methods (may add thin helpers).  
3. Change `SQLiteStore` / `PGStore` / `MemoryStore` methods to either:
   - **Facade:** call shared policy then dialect persist (temporary), or  
   - **Delegate:** `return claimService.Claim(...)` if service is injectable (harder for storage package).  

Prefer **policy package in `core/` or `app/services` + thin store writes** so `storage` does not import `app` (dependency direction: app → storage only).

Correct direction:

```
app/services  →  core transitions (pure)
app/services  →  storage.Store (CRUD)
storage/*     →  core transitions (optional, for facade during migration only)
storage/*  ̸→  app  (forbidden)
```

If store facades need shared rules during migration, put pure functions in `core/smart_contract` or keep them in `storage/smart_contract` helpers (already started with `proposal_prepare.go`) and move upward when app owns the call path.

### Transaction boundaries

Claim/Approve need multi-row atomicity. Options:

1. **Store methods stay transactional** but only run SQL produced after pure decision (service returns a `ClaimPlan{insert claim, update task, ...}`; store applies plan in one tx).  
2. **Store exposes `RunInTx(fn)`** + row-level ops; service owns the fn (cleaner long-term; more API surface).

Recommend **option 1 for Wave 1** (less interface churn), **option 2 for Wave 2+** if plan types get large.

### Status transition tables (document in code)

Codify once (today’s behavior — verify against all three stores before “fixing”):

**Task:** `available` → `claimed` → (`submitted`/`pending_review`) → `approved` | back to `available` on reject  
**Claim:** `active` → `submitted`/`complete`/`rejected`; same wallet re-claim of active is idempotent  
**Proposal:** `pending` → `approved` → `published`; sibling pendings for same wish/contract → `rejected` on approve  
**Contract/wish:** never supersede/demote `confirmed`/`completed` via proposal create or approval (see `supersedeEligibleStatusSQL` / contract protection)

### Test strategy

- **Pure unit tests** for each transition (table-driven).  
- **One integration suite** run against Memory + SQLite (temp file); PG optional in CI if DSN present.  
- Reuse/expand: `sqlite_store_test.go`, `proposal_*_test.go`, `auth_security_test.go`, contract protection tests.  
- Golden rule: for each extracted method, assert Memory/SQLite/PG produce same error sentinels (`ErrTaskTaken`, `ErrTaskUnavailable`, …) and same resulting row statuses.

### Call-site migration

After services own policy:

| Caller | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `app/smart_contract/server_*.go` | already uses services for some paths — ensure claim/submit go through ClaimService |
| `mcp/*` | call services (or app Server ports), not fat store methods |
| sync (ingestion/ipfs/stego) | keep using `UpsertContractWithTasks` but via ContractService once protection lives there |

### Success metric

- Lines of **behavioral** code in the three stores drop sharply (target: each store method for Wave 1–2 is mostly SQL).  
- Zero intentional behavior differences between dialects for extracted methods (enforced by shared tests).  
- `stargate-jh0` can implement a single GORM repo for rows without re-encoding approve/claim rules.

## Acceptance criteria

### Functional
- [ ] **ClaimTask:** available/claimed gates, ErrTaskTaken for other wallet, same-wallet idempotent reclaim, claim TTL applied, contractor_wallet written to merkle_proof — one shared implementation; all three dialects pass the same tests
- [ ] **SubmitWork:** rejects non-active/expired claims consistently; creates submission; updates claim/task status identically across dialects
- [ ] **UpdateSubmissionStatus:** approve/reject cascades (task + claim) implemented once; SubmissionService uses it without dialect branches
- [ ] **ApproveProposal:** pending-only; ValidateProposalForApproval; reject sibling pendings for same contract/pixel hash; block dual approve/publish; never supersede confirmed/completed wish contracts
- [ ] **PublishProposal:** requires approved (or already published); task/claim bulk transitions match current product behavior
- [ ] **CreateProposal:** PrepareProposalForCreate path; supersede rules preserved
- [ ] REST + MCP claim/submit/approve/publish paths go through app services (no new call sites that reimplement policy in handlers)

### Structural
- [ ] Pure transition helpers live outside dialect files (`core/smart_contract` and/or `app/.../services`)
- [ ] `storage` does not import `app`
- [ ] No new triplicated policy blocks in `sqlite_store` / `pg_store` / `memory_store` for extracted methods (facade OK if thin)
- [ ] Document status transition table in code comments or `docs/history/`

### Quality
- [ ] `go test ./storage/smart_contract/ ./app/smart_contract/...` pass
- [ ] No intentional behavior change vs pre-refactor (regression tests cover claim conflict, approve conflict, confirmed-wish protection)
- [ ] Follow-up `stargate-jh0` unblocked for at least Claim/Proposal row CRUD (comment when ready)

### Non-goals (must not block close)
- Full GORM migration of MCP tables
- Deleting MemoryStore
- Perfect Store interface minimization (can leave unused fat methods as thin wrappers until jh0)

title: Publishing a wish leaves two contract rows and LookupContract by wish id returns the stale one
description:
Publishing a proposal upserts a contract whose row id comes from the proposal's metadata contract_id (app/smart_contract/services/event_service.go:57, via ContractIDFromMeta). For wish proposals that value is the bare 64-char hash, because ProposalService.Create requires contract_id == visible_pixel_hash. The wish itself is stored as wish-<hash>. UpsertContractWithTasks does not normalize the id, so publish inserts a second row rather than updating the wish.

Verified against MemoryStore: after seeding wish-<hash> (status pending) and publishing with the bare hash, ListContracts returns both rows -- wish-<hash> pending and <hash> active.

The part that is not merely cosmetic: LookupContract(wish-<hash>) resolves to the STALE pending row, not the published active one. Lookups by wish id therefore report a published wish as unpublished, and any listing shows the same wish twice.

Pre-existing on the REST path; not introduced by stargate-fhz. Before fhz, MCP wrote contract_id as wish-<hash>, so publishes from that surface happened to upsert the wish row in place and avoided this. Aligning MCP onto the service in #21 means MCP-created wishes now take the same path REST always did, which is correct for consistency but widens the exposure of this bug.

Raised by Maya in review of #21, who traced the mechanism and judged it alignment rather than a new hole. That is right. The stale-row lookup is the part worth fixing separately.

Fix direction: normalize the contract row id through identity.ToWishID when the proposal is a wish proposal, so publish updates wish-<hash> in place. Needs a decision on rows already written in the bare-hash shape, since #21 explicitly did not migrate historical data.
design: Canonical stored contract id is the bare 64-hex VPH. wish- is a lookup alias only. New writes (ingest, publish, confirm, stego) persist the bare hash. Confirm updates the row it finds and must not copy onto wish-. If a later write sees only wish- and no bare sibling, adopt that row onto the bare PK (remap tasks, supersede the prefix row). If both exist, keep the live row (usually bare active/confirmed) and supersede the leftover wish- pending twin. Reads keep CandidateIDs forever.
close_reason: Canonical stored contract id is now the bare VPH. wish- is a lookup alias. New writes (ingest, publish, confirm, stego, inscription, MCP PSBT lookup) persist or resolve the bare hash. Confirm/publish adopt a wish-only leftover onto that PK and supersede the prefix twin. LookupContract and list collapse pick the live row. ADR 0003 and DOMAIN_SEAMS updated. go test ./... green.

irl.1 review, so please read this before reopening either:

1. manifest.Issuer is not the creator. It is STARGATE_STEGO_ISSUER /
   INSTANCE_ID / hostname / "stargate" (stego_publish.go:78-87), a node label
   validated only as non-empty (stego/manifest.go:34); fixtures use "oracle-1"
   and "tester". Using it would let any replicating node approve payouts on
   every wish it mirrors.

2. Do not copy creator_wallet from the stego payload, even fill-if-absent.
   extractStegoMetadata has no allowlist (stego_publish.go:830-848) so the
   field is embedded on publish, but inbound it is attacker-controlled and is
   deliberately excluded from stegoPayloadMetadataAllowlist
   (stego_security.go:19-27). Two consequences:
     - ensureStegoIngestion calls UpdateFromIngest when the row exists
       (stego_reconcile.go:439-441), and that merges incoming-wins on both
       dialects (mergeMetadataSQLite existing[k]=v service.go:572-574;
       postgres metadata || $6 service.go:411). A crafted replica of an
       existing wish would therefore overwrite the real creator_wallet on the
       origin node, making the attacker the recorded owner.
     - Fill-if-absent only narrows this to first-writer-wins, and on a fresh
       peer the attacker can be first.

The on-chain gate does not supply the missing binding. parseOPReturnHashes
reads wish_hash || stego_hash (block_monitor_reconcile.go:265-273) and
reconcileStegoFromLocalFile rejects a hash mismatch
(stego_reconcile.go:174-179), so the chain binds the image BYTES to the
inscription. But contractID comes from manifest.VisiblePixelHash
(stego_reconcile.go:194), and the no-candidate branch materializes a contract
for a wish the node has never seen (block_monitor_reconcile.go:331-356). No
step extracts a funding input address or ties either hash to a wallet.

What would actually close it: a signature over the wish hash by the creator's
key, carried alongside the wish and verified independently of the payload, so
a replica can check authorship without trusting the carrier. That is a
protocol change and needs a decision on where the signature lives and which
key signs.

Also worth resolving as part of the design: whether Global Auditor should
remain a blanket approver, which stargate-irl.2 already flags.

Do not implement by relaxing the fail-closed rule. If replica approval is
urgent before this lands, Global Auditor is the intended path.

Discussed in #stargate; cursor-agent proposed (1), maya proposed (2), both
withdrawn after tracing the inbound path.
close_reason: Creator attestation protocol: Bitcoin signed message over STARLIGHT-WISH-V1 + wish hash, carried as first-class stego fields (not payload.Metadata). Replicas verify on chain-apply and SetCreatorWalletIfAbsent; origin attest via POST /api/inscriptions/{id}/attest. Issuer and unsigned creator_wallet copies remain untrusted. Fail-closed unchanged. Global Auditor left as this node's settlement wallet. ADR 0007. Tests: verify, overwrite, unverified claim, replica approve, REST attest, WishChat record signature.

title: Sandbox tarball extraction has no size or entry-count limit (decompression bomb)
description:
backend/app/smart_contract/stego_reconcile.go:924  data, err := io.ReadAll(tr)

Unbounded read per tar entry, with no cap on total extracted bytes, per-file size, or entry count. This tarball arrives from peers and is referenced by on-chain commitments, so the content is attacker-supplied: a small stego payload can point at a tarball that exhausts memory or fills the disk on every node that reconciles the block.

Credit where due: the same loop handles tar.TypeReg only, so symlink and hardlink attacks are already closed.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: Extraction enforces a max per-entry size, max total extracted bytes, and max entry count via io.LimitReader, aborting and logging when exceeded. Limits are configurable with safe defaults. Test covers an oversized entry and an excessive entry count.
notes: Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). Confirmed by room, agreed as a cheap win to do today. Scope note: while adding the size and entry-count caps, also fix the HasPrefix-without-separator check at stego_reconcile.go:916 in this same loop (the extraction-path instance of irl.5). maya also confirmed the TypeReg-only handling is already correct, so symlinks need no work here.
close_reason:
Landed on dev. Verified on origin/dev stego_reconcile.go: sandboxMaxEntries 4096, sandboxMaxFileBytes 32 MiB, sandboxMaxTotalBytes 256 MiB. All three requested caps are present.

Details worth recording. headerCount increments on every header before the type and size filters, so skipped entries cannot be used to exceed the entry cap. Per-file size is checked twice, at hdr.Size and again on the body via io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(tr, max+1)) with a len check, which is correct because a header can understate the body. The total-bytes pre-check uses declared hdr.Size while the accumulator adds actual len(data), which looks like a hole for entries that lie small and are then skipped without counting, but Go's tar.Reader caps an entry read at the declared size, so a small declared size yields a short read and no amplification. Traversal goes through security.SanitizePath and only tar.TypeReg is written, so the symlink/hardlink surface stays closed.

title: "Global Auditor" names a per-instance oracle identity as if it were network-wide
description:
PlanEnvSeed (storage/auth/apikey_store.go:190-193) binds STARGATE_API_KEY to STARLIGHT_DONATION_ADDRESS whenever both are set, which is the normal production configuration. isGlobalAuditor (app/smart_contract/authz.go:84) then matches that wallet, and Authorize returns at line 47 BEFORE any creator check.

Verified empirically with both env vars set and a real seeded key store:

  admin key present=true wallet="bc1qdonation"
  Authorize(admin-key, wish) -> wallet="bc1qdonation" err=<nil>
  ... against a wish whose recorded creator_wallet is bc1qsomeoneelse

Because every gate built during the authz work funnels through WishCreatorAuthorizer.Authorize, one key bypasses all of them: proposal edit and publish (irl.7), proposal approve (az6), submission review (ugs), submission rework (hs2), contract rework requests (irl.8), and the MCP equivalents (fhz). The creator-only, fail-closed property those changes established holds for every key except this one.

Not necessarily a bug -- an operator escape hatch is defensible, and removing it outright would make replicated wishes unapprovable by anyone, which is exactly what stargate-6ds is about. What is not defensible is that it is silent and on by default: any deployment that sets a donation address to receive sweeps also, as a side effect, turns its admin key into a universal approver. Nothing in the config says so and no log line reports a use.

The audit trail is at least honest: Authorize returns the auditor wallet, so events record bc1qdonation rather than impersonating the creator.

Needs a decision before a fix (see stargate-6ds item 3, they should be resolved together):
  a. keep as-is and document it
  b. keep but require a separate explicit opt-in variable, and log every bypass
  c. narrow it so it cannot approve payouts, only dispute/rework paths
  d. remove it and let 6ds's signature scheme cover replicas

Found while confirming 6ds against the code.
notes:
CORRECTIONS after maya re-derived this. Two claims in the description above are wrong; the core chain holds.

1. WRONG: 'all six creator gates'. hs2 is not on this path. SubmissionReworkGate (authz_rework.go:32) compares the bound wallet to claim.AiIdentifier and never calls WishCreatorAuthorizer.Authorize -- verified, zero references to WishCreatorAuthorizer, isGlobalAuditor or the donation env in that file. The admin key cannot rework another agent's submission unless it is the claimant. Affected: proposal edit/publish (irl.7), approve (az6), submission review (ugs), rework requests (irl.8), create_task via AuthorizeContractOwner, and the MCP equivalents (fhz). Five, not six.

2. WRONG: 'silent and no log line reports a use', and 'nothing in the config says so'. Both false. authz.go:48 logs every bypass ('AUTHORIZATION: Allowing %s based on Global Auditor status'), and AGENTS.md documents STARLIGHT_DONATION_ADDRESS as giving 'the agent global auditor powers for approvals'.

What is actually undocumented is the COUPLING, and that is the real finding: README and starlight_contracts.md present the variable as a P2WPKH sweep destination, while PlanEnvSeed makes that same address the wallet of the seeded admin key. Setting a donation address so sweeps have a destination is what promotes STARGATE_API_KEY to universal approver. Nothing ties those two documents together.

3. NARROWER TRIGGER than stated: it needs BOTH variables. Donation-only does not bypass, verified:

  donation-as-key present=true wallet=""
  DONATION-ONLY Authorize -> err=api key with wallet binding required to approve the submission
  TWO-VAR       key wallet="bc1qdonation" Authorize -> wallet="bc1qdonation" err=<nil>

SeedDonationAsKey writes no wallet, so boundWallet is empty and Authorize refuses before isGlobalAuditor is consulted.

4. Second copy of the same rule, not a gate: inscription_handler.go:746, wish delete, a local EqualFold against the env var.

RECOMMENDATION, maya's and now mine: split the knobs rather than document the coupling. STARLIGHT_DONATION_ADDRESS stays the money sink; auditor becomes an explicit second variable, or goes. Keep-and-document leaves the footgun in place. Removing outright is coherent only if replicated wishes being unapprovable on this node is acceptable, which is stargate-6ds.

Also pre-existing test coverage: TestWishCreatorAuthorizerAllowsGlobalAuditor already pins the bypass -- stranger key, no ingest record, donation env set, allowed, returning the auditor wallet. The behaviour was intended and tested; the coupling is what nobody chose.
RESOLVED BY ERIC. This is not a security issue and there is no decision to make. My framing was wrong; recording the correct model.

Eric: STARGATE_API_KEY is the credential Starlight uses to call back into Stargate to ingest data as an oracle. Each Starlight instance has its OWN STARGATE_API_KEY and its OWN donation address, so the pair is per-instance: whichever instance worked the contract is the one the donation goes to. There is no universal global auditor.

So the intended model is that a node's oracle identity can settle work on that node. It is an authorized settlement actor, not a super-user, and the creator gates it skips are gates on OTHER callers. Nothing is bypassed that was meant to apply to it.

Where I went wrong, because it is worth recording: isGlobalAuditor reads os.Getenv("STARLIGHT_DONATION_ADDRESS") from the Stargate node's own environment, so the comparison is node-local by construction. The doc comment directly above it says 'node-wide approver' and is correct. I read the identifier name, called the scope global, and did not reconcile that against the comment two lines up -- after spending the evening fixing comments that stated superseded rules, I took a NAME at face value instead of deriving the scope from the code. The env read was in front of me in the same function.

What remains, and it is Eric's own point ('how it is tied to donation address is the cause of confusion'): the naming and the coupling mislead readers.

  - isGlobalAuditor / 'Global Auditor' describes a per-instance oracle as network-wide. The word global is the whole problem.
  - AGENTS.md says the variable 'gives the agent global auditor powers for approvals', repeating it.
  - One variable carries two meanings: the sweep/donation destination and the oracle wallet identity. Reading either doc alone does not reveal the other.

Scope now: rename and document, no behaviour change. P1 -> P3.
REVISIT 2026-09-14 (Eric): GGUF in-process vs STARGATE_API_KEY.

Original microservice job is gone. Image scan init is Trin/GGUF → Alpha → Mock (scanner_manager.go). NewProxyScanner is unreferenced. Inbound IPFS ingest is no longer "Starlight oracle callbacks with STARGATE_API_KEY":
  - /api/ingest-* uses STARGATE_INGEST_TOKEN (fail-closed, irl.3)
  - /api/stego/callback uses STARLIGHT_CALLBACK_SECRET HMAC (fail-closed, irl.3)
  - replica ingest is block monitor + local hash files + IPFS mirror

STARGATE_API_KEY still does three leftover jobs:
  1. Optional outbound Bearer on STARGATE_PROXY_BASE /inscribe and /scan/image (legacy sidecar; native extract/embed is default when unset)
  2. Operator seed into api_keys (MCP/REST bootstrap without challenge/verify)
  3. When paired with STARLIGHT_DONATION_ADDRESS, wallet-bind that seed → isGlobalAuditor (node-local settlement hatch for 6ds replicas)

Scan/GGUF does not need (1). (2) is convenience, not architecture. (3) is the remaining privilege and the 2f6 naming/coupling problem.

Exposure: leaking the seeded key is a node-admin problem iff it is bound to the donation wallet (approve/edit/review/delete on this node). It is not a network-wide auditor. Key-only seed has no wallet, so Authorize refuses it. Docs still describe the var as "if scanner requires auth", which understates (3) and overstates (1).

Recommended decision (stronger than rename-and-document):
  - Do not keep STARGATE_API_KEY for scanning.
  - Split or drop the auditor coupling; leave 6ds as the replica-approval protocol.
  - Keep an optional operator seed only if we still want a non-wallet bootstrap key, under a name that does not imply scanner/oracle.
  - Retire DEPLOYMENT.md / README scanner-auth wording and the unused ProxyScanner path.
close_reason: Removed STARGATE_API_KEY as an unverified login. Env seed no longer inserts a key (warn-only if leftover). Outbound proxy Bearer gone. Keys issued only by challenge/verify. isGlobalAuditor renamed to isDonationWallet and now requires a verified key bound to STARLIGHT_DONATION_ADDRESS. Replica approval remains stargate-6ds.

title: An empty creator_wallet counts as a known creator, so the denial blames the caller's key
description:
inscription_handler.go:584 writes creator_wallet unconditionally, including when it resolved to the empty string (no creator key on the request, unknown key, or a key with no wallet binding -- lines 568-573 leave creatorWallet empty and nothing guards the write).

wishOwnership then does a plain string type assertion (authz.go:124), and "" is a string, so ok is true and known becomes true with creator == "".

Verified against the real IngestionService and WishCreatorAuthorizer:

  row metadata {"creator_wallet": ""}  -> known=true  creator=""
     Authorize -> 'approver wallet bc1qstranger does not match wish creator'

  row metadata {} (key absent)         -> known=false creator=""
     Authorize -> 'cannot approve ...: no creator wallet recorded for wish bb11...'

Not a security bug: both deny, and the empty creator can never EqualFold a bound wallet, so the wish is unapprovable by everyone except the Global Auditor. It is a diagnostic bug. The first message asserts a creator exists and that the caller used the wrong key, which sends an operator looking for the right key when the real problem is that the wish was ingested without creator identity. The second message is the accurate one and is what this case should produce.

Fix: treat an empty creator_wallet as not-established in wishOwnership, so it falls through to the replicated / no-creator-recorded messages. Decision is unchanged in every case; only the message improves. Optionally also stop writing the key when the value is empty, though reading defensively is the load-bearing half since existing rows already carry it.

Found while confirming stargate-6ds against the code.
notes:
HISTORY. This is a record of what this bead's close reason said before, not a description of it now. The reason above is maintained and is the single place the sequence and the tally live -- deliberately not repeated here, because that duplication is what kept going stale.

The original reason claimed the follow-up comment fix a629df3 was on dev.
