Maya caught it three times running, and the pattern in the catches is the useful part. First the reason asserted a commit was on dev without checking ancestry. Then, once the reason was fixed, this note still opened by quoting a sentence that no longer existed above it. Then this note carried a running count and a commit reference that the next fix invalidated. Each correction created the next staleness, because the same fact was written in two places and only one got updated.

The durable lesson, kept in the reason rather than duplicated: a push to a merged PR's branch reports success and lands nowhere, so 'the PR merged' is not the same claim as 'my commit landed', and only ancestry of the specific commit settles it. title: bd close --reason on an already-closed issue reports success and silently discards the reason
description:
Running 'bd close <id> --reason "..."' against an issue that is already closed prints the success line, including the new reason echoed back:

  ✓ Closed stargate-z6k — <title>: Landed as a1bf16e + 860b5c5 in PR #26, merged to dev as 51a769d. One switch...

but close_reason is not updated. Verified with bd 1.2.2: exported before and after, the row was byte-identical and still carried the original reason. The stale text survived and shipped to dev, where it stated behaviour that had been superseded within the same PR.

There is also no way to correct it afterwards: 'bd update' has no --reason flag, so the only routes are reopen-then-close or 'bd update --append-notes'. Used append-notes here since it does not churn status.

Impact is that a wrong close_reason is durable and looks corrected when it is not. Same family as stargate-kp5 (a command that appeared to work but did not do the thing).

Fix: either update close_reason when close is called on an already-closed issue, or refuse with a message saying it is already closed and the reason was not applied. Silent discard behind a success line is the bad case. A --reason flag on bd update would also cover it.

Found while correcting the z6k close_reason after PR #28.
notes:
WORKAROUND, verified. A wrong close reason can be corrected despite this bug:

  bd update <id> -s open
  bd close <id> --reason "<corrected text>"

--reason is honoured on the re-close because the issue is open at that moment. Checked field-by-field on stargate-b11: close_reason is replaced, notes survive byte-for-byte (1135 chars before and after), status returns to closed. Only close_reason, closed_at and updated_at move, so closed_at is rewritten to the correction time and the original close time is lost -- the one cost.

This is better than the --append-notes workaround recorded earlier, because the false text is removed from the field a reader sees first rather than contradicted further down. Use append-notes only when the original reason should be preserved as a record.

Does not change the bug: bd close --reason on an already-closed issue still reports success and discards the reason silently, which is the actual defect. It should either apply the reason or fail loudly.

title: Path confinement uses HasPrefix without a separator in 4 places instead of security.SanitizePath
description:
The repo already has a correct helper -- security.SanitizePath compares against baseDir+string(filepath.Separator) (backend/security/path_sanitizer.go:53) -- but four call sites hand-roll a weaker check:

  backend/stargate_backend.go:153   /uploads/  handler
  backend/stargate_backend.go:764   /sandbox/  handler
  backend/stargate_backend.go:968   block-image uploads fallback
  backend/app/smart_contract/stego_reconcile.go:916  tar entry output path

Verified reachable: Go's ServeMux 301-redirects a literal '..' segment, but percent-encoded forms ('/uploads/..%2fsibling%2ffile', '/uploads/%2e%2e/...') survive mux cleaning and arrive at the handler with '../' intact in r.URL.Path, and the prefix check passes.

Severity is limited rather than critical: UPLOADS_DIR is defaulted to data/uploads (stargate_backend.go:392), so an escape only reaches sibling directories that share that string prefix, and none exist in the default or Docker layouts. Filing as a real but latent bug -- it is one config change away from mattering and the correct helper is already available.

Note: /api/block-image/{height}/{filename} was investigated and is NOT vulnerable -- strings.Split on the already-decoded r.URL.Path (stargate_backend.go:937) means filename can never contain a separator, encoded or not.

Discovered during a full-repo code review on 2026-09-13 (build clean, `go test ./...` green across all 25 packages).
acceptance_criteria: All four sites route through security.SanitizePath (or an equivalent separator-aware check). Table test covers percent-encoded traversal ('..%2f', '%2e%2e') and the sibling-prefix case (uploads vs uploads-backup).
notes: Triaged in #stargate chat 2026-09-13 with maya (independent code read, claims re-verified locally). DEPRIORITIZED as a standalone project (P2 -> P3) by room consensus, but NOT dropped. maya's point: the fourth instance of this bug is inside the tarball extraction path (stego_reconcile.go:916), which is exactly the code irl.6 already has to touch to add size caps. So fix that one instance as part of irl.6 and leave the three HTTP-serving instances (stargate_backend.go:153, :764, :968) here as lower-priority cleanup. Agreed rationale: no node is publicly exposed yet, and impact is bounded to sibling directories sharing the path prefix.
close_reason: Landed on dev via Maya's PR #20 after PR #18 merged an older commit without the table cases. Verified on origin/dev: stargate_backend_test.go carries TestCustomUploadsHandlerRejectsEncodedTraversal. Cases were mutation-checked against the pre-fix HasPrefix logic and all leaked content without the fix. Uppercase %2E%2E is intentionally absent: net/http percent-decodes r.URL.Path before the handler runs, so it is the same input as %2e%2e.

title: maybeConfirmContract should re-run sandbox reconcile after delayed confirm
description:
4u5 added promoteFundedContracts -> ConfirmContract + reconcileOnChainArtifacts for status=funded. The task-proof path (promoteProvisionalProofs -> maybeConfirmContract) still only ConfirmContract. A contract that confirms only via task proofs still misses the delayed sandbox extract retry (1-conf reconcile skipped download because the contract was not confirmed yet).

Do not mix into the 4u5 offset paging patch.
acceptance_criteria: After maybeConfirmContract succeeds, re-run reconcileOnChainArtifacts when a stego hash is available (same keys as contractStegoHash). Test: task-proof confirm path invokes sandbox/stego reconcile.
close_reason:
Landed on dev via PR #32 (872f8f7, merge 18607b5). Verified on origin/dev: reconcileConfirmedContractArtifacts is present and promoteProvisionalProofs calls it once per contract id after maybeConfirmContract reports a confirm.

The gap: reconcile only spawns the sandbox extract when the contract row already reads confirmed, and at one confirmation it does not yet, so that pass reconciled the stego image and skipped the extract. 4u5 covered the funded and OP_RETURN scan paths; the task-proof path confirmed and stopped, so a contract that only ever confirmed through task proofs never extracted its tarball.

maybeConfirmContract now returns whether the confirm was attempted without error, which previously could not be distinguished from a settlement-not-ready bail. Deliberately not hoisted into maybeConfirmContract: the scan path's OP_RETURN hash is authoritative before the row carries it, so folding it in would trade a working path for symmetry.

Review follow-up 872f8f7 removed a duplicate function-local contractGetter and corrected the bool's doc comment, which had claimed it reports whether the contract was 'actually confirmed'. It reports no-error: for an absent row MemoryStore returns not-found but SQLStore updates zero rows and returns nil, and production runs SQLStore. That divergence is inherited and intentionally not filed; the production path re-reads and no-ops.
